BLOCKER: Flow checklist marks a stage `[DONE]` whenever it has any event, including a latest status of `fail`; the `[BLOCKED]` branch is unreachable because `blocked` is only ever a stage that *has* a failing event, yet the `if not ev:` guard skips it. A failed `gate0`/`tests` renders "[DONE] gate0 (fail)" and `current_stage` says "blocked at gate0" — the checklist contradicts the header and hides the stop.

Same bug for reviews: a design/diff review left at `fail`/NOT READY shows "[DONE] design_review (NOT READY)" and current stage jumps to `gate1`, presenting an unresolved NOT READY as finished. Tests only cover the fail-then-pass path, so this is untested and uncaught.
MAJOR: `_parse_recommendation` accepts any uppercase run as the recommendation instead of validating against the canonical set (APPROVE / APPROVE WITH ATTENTION / NOT READY). A line like "Overall architect recommendation: APPROVE - 3 ITEMS NEED ATTENTION" normalizes to a bogus "recommendation" that the checklist then displays as authoritative status.

`current_stage` returns three different string shapes ("gate1", "blocked at gate0", "complete") from one function; callers (checklist, final table, future consumers) must string-match. Also, any closed-status item with missing pre-merge stages reports "complete", masking incomplete work.

`show` now runs two synchronous subprocesses (20s each) on every invocation for a read-only view; the render path is coupled to scraping CLI prose from `architect_review.py` rather than a structured evidence API. Any refactor of the review renderer silently degrades `show` to "evidence missing".
MINOR: Timeout cut from 60s to 20s with no rationale; a slow evidence render now yields a misleading "(evidence missing)" instead of the real table.
`--item` value is passed straight into a subprocess argv; an item id beginning with "-" is argument injection into `architect_review.py`.
`id-blocks.json` allocator bookkeeping (two scopes, `reserved_up_to` 1073→1186 with unaccounted gaps) is bundled into a feature PR — mixed concerns and noisy history for a single-writer file.
`CLOSED_STATUSES` and the review-stage set are inline string literals; they will drift from `core.backlog`/`architect_review` vocabularies without a shared constant.
NIT: Section numbers ("## 1." … "## 11.") are hard-coded in headings, docs, and test assertions; renumbering breaks three places.
Recommendation regex char class `[A-Z][A-Z0-9 _/-]*` should be anchored to end-of-line to avoid capturing trailing uppercase prose.
`runs.get(stage, 1)` default and the unused `known`/`extra` handling are subtle; a legacy-stage event that is also the latest could double-display logic paths.
SUMMARY: Solid structure: sections in AC order, disposition key, review-recommendation-not-ingest-status, re-run dedupe, empty/partial item coverage, and docs invariants are all present and well tested — but the headline AC ("flow checklist with the current stage") is broken for the failure path.
Top risk: the checklist reports failed and NOT-READY stages as [DONE] with an unreachable [BLOCKED] marker; fix the mark logic and add fail-path tests before merge.
Second risk: unvalidated regex scraping of the review CLI as the source of truth for recommendations; validate against the canonical enum and prefer structured evidence over subprocess text.
